newsitem.title: FRANCE: FFSA plan new appeal against post office tax break.
newsitem.headline: FFSA plan new appeal against post office tax break.

text.p: The French federation of insurance companies (FFSA) said on Friday five French insurance groups planned to take their appeal against a tax break given to the state post office to the European Court of Justice.

The statement came the day after the European Court of First Instance turned down a similar appeal, saying the tax advantage was acceptable under European Union rules on state aid as it helped the post office meet its public service obligations.
The FFSA said in a statement the tax advantage was in the eyes of the insurance groups a "competitive distortion."
The groups are challenging a law introduced in July 1990 whiich allows the post office, La Poste, to offer insurance services and gives them a reduced rate for paying local taxes.

The Court of First Instance supported the European Commission, which found that the tax concession was less than the economic burden of La Poste's public-interest tasks, such as the obligation to operate post offices in unprofitable rural areas.

The ruling was seen as a setback to private operators that have been trying to curtail the power of postal monopolies across the EU, which has so far taken a go-slow approach to liberalising the sector.
